data.title: Electricals
data.heroDescription: Comprehensive electrical services for commercial and industrial facilities, from installation to maintenance to emergency response
data.overview:
Electrical systems are critical infrastructure. A fault isn't just a cost — it affects operations, safety, and compliance. Atlas South provides end-to-end electrical services: planned maintenance, rapid fault diagnosis, emergency response, and full compliance testing.

Our engineers are qualified to Building Regulations, BS 7909, and all relevant electrical standards. We manage everything from routine PAT testing to major system upgrades.

features.title: Planned Maintenance
features.description: Scheduled inspections, testing, and maintenance to catch faults before they cause failures.

features.title: Installation & Upgrades
features.description: New circuits, panel upgrades, lighting refits, and complete system rewiring for renovations.

features.title: Emergency Response
features.description: Rapid dispatch for electrical faults, outages, and safety issues causing downtime.

features.title: Compliance & Testing
features.description: EICR inspections, PAT testing, isolation device testing, all with full documentation.

features.title: Fault Diagnosis
features.description: Thermal imaging, circuit tracing, and specialist equipment to diagnose intermittent or complex issues.

features.title: Energy Optimization
features.description: LED retrofits, sensor controls, and load optimization to reduce electricity bills.

faqs.question: What electrical work requires a qualified engineer?
faqs.answer: Most commercial work does. Building Regulations requires Part P qualified engineers for new circuits, distribution board work, and high-risk modifications. We are fully qualified and insured.

faqs.question: How often do EICR inspections need doing?
faqs.answer: BS 7909 recommends every 3–5 years for most commercial buildings. High-use facilities may need annual inspections. We assess your building to recommend the right interval.

faqs.question: What if an engineer finds something during testing?
faqs.answer: We categorize faults by risk (C1 = immediate, C2 = planned, C3 = advisory). We provide a full report with remedial quotations so you can plan budget.

faqs.question: Can you work without shutting down the building?
faqs.answer: Yes. We use temporary supplies, phased work schedules, and non-disruptive testing techniques to minimize impact during maintenance.

faqs.question: Do you do small jobs or only big installations?
faqs.answer: Both. From single-circuit additions to major system overhauls, we handle projects of any size with the same quality and compliance standard.

data.title: Reactive Maintenance

We respond to call-outs from emergency repairs (broken doors, burst pipes, electrical faults) to complex multi-trade issues. A dedicated control room manages dispatch to hit response-time targets even during peak demand.

features.title: 24/7 Hotline
features.description: Call any time, day or night. Qualified engineers dispatched to your location within response time commitment.

features.title: Multi-Trade Capability

features.title: Rapid Diagnosis

features.title: Stock & Spares

features.title: Breakdown Prevention

faqs.question: What counts as a reactive maintenance emergency?
faqs.answer: Anything affecting operations or safety: equipment failure, burst pipes, electrical faults, door locks, HVAC breakdown, etc. We respond to all call-outs equally.

faqs.question: How much does a reactive call cost?
faqs.answer: Call-out and first hour: fixed rate. Additional labor: hourly rate. Materials at cost + markup. We provide estimates before starting work exceeding the first-hour rate.

faqs.question: Can you start work before my approval?
faqs.answer: For safety emergencies (electrical hazard, water leak, broken security), yes — we act first and explain after. For non-urgent issues, we always get approval and cost estimate first.

faqs.question: Is reactive maintenance covered under a maintenance contract?
faqs.answer: Depends on the contract. Some contracts bundle reactives; others separate emergency call-out costs. We can structure contracts however suits your budget and risk profile.

faqs.question: Do you help with insurance claims for equipment damage?
faqs.answer: Yes. We document everything and provide detailed reports that help with insurer claims. Many clients have us on speed-dial specifically for claims support.

data.title: Fire & Safety
data.heroDescription: Comprehensive fire safety, emergency lighting, and life-safety systems to keep your building code-compliant and people protected
data.overview:
Fire safety isn't optional—it's a legal duty and a moral imperative. Fire Safety Order 2005 requires regular testing, maintenance, and certification. Atlas South manages the full scope: sprinkler systems, emergency lighting, fire alarms, evacuation procedures, and compliance records.

We work with fire safety engineers, local authorities, and insurers to ensure your building meets all statutory requirements and your team understands emergency protocols.

features.title: Sprinkler Systems
features.description: Installation, testing, and annual certification of fire sprinkler systems per BS 9251 and insurance requirements.

features.title: Emergency Lighting
features.description: Testing, maintenance, and battery replacement for emergency lighting and exit signage systems.

features.title: Fire Alarm Systems
features.description: Design, installation, testing, and ongoing maintenance of fire detection and alarm systems.

features.title: Evacuation Planning
features.description: Risk assessment, evacuation route planning, assembly point setup, and staff training programs.

features.title: Compliance & Audit
features.description: Full compliance audits against Fire Safety Order, Building Regulations, and insurance requirements.

features.title: Documentation
features.description: Comprehensive maintenance records, test certificates, and compliance reports for insurers and authorities.

faqs.question: What tests do fire safety systems need?
faqs.answer: Sprinklers annually (BS 9251); emergency lighting monthly walkthrough + annual full test; fire alarms weekly/monthly depending on system type. We schedule and document everything.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for fire safety compliance?
faqs.answer: The building owner and occupier have a joint duty under Fire Safety Order 2005. We help you meet that duty through testing, training, and documentation.

faqs.question: What if your tests find a fault?
faqs.answer: We report the fault, recommend remedial action, and provide quotations for repairs. Critical faults (failed sprinkler test, non-functional alarm) must be fixed before re-use.

faqs.question: Do you help with fire safety training?
faqs.answer: We coordinate with accredited fire training providers. We can arrange on-site drill training and evacuation exercises tailored to your building layout.

faqs.question: Are fire safety costs covered by insurance?
faqs.answer: No, fire safety compliance is a legal requirement, not an insurance-covered item. However, lapses in fire safety can void insurance, so staying compliant protects you.

data.title: Corporate
data.heroDescription: Multi-site compliance, predictable costs, and responsive support for enterprise building management
data.overview:
Corporate headquarters and multi-site office portfolios demand building services that don't just react to problems — they anticipate them. Your facilities underpin business continuity, employee safety, and regulatory compliance across often-complex estate profiles.

Atlas South has supported corporate clients from FTSE-listed firms to growth-stage tech companies, managing everything from routine maintenance schedules to emergency response coordination across multiple buildings, often across multiple regions.
data.challenges:
- **Spread-out sites:** Managing 5, 10, or 50+ sites means coordinating maintenance, compliance, and emergency response across locations — without creating a procurement nightmare.
- **Regulatory weight:** Health & Safety, Fire Safety, electrical testing, water safety — the compliance calendar never stops. A missed inspection or certification lapse carries real liability.
- **Cost control:** Building services budgets need predictability and visibility. Reactive repairs eat contingency; poor preventative planning wastes money.
- **Tenant/employee safety:** Any service failure is not just a cost — it affects day-to-day operations and employee experience.
- **Partner coordination:** Juggling multiple service providers across sites creates coordination overhead and the risk of gaps where "we thought the other vendor was handling that."
data.ourApproach:
We consolidate your building services under a single partner, reducing the overhead of managing multiple vendors. For corporate clients, we typically structure a combination of:

- **Preventative maintenance contracts** with fixed annual costs and clearly scheduled works, so you know what to budget and what's covered.
- **24/7 emergency response** for unplanned breakdowns — one call, one dispatcher, engineers deployed to whichever site needs them.
- **Compliance management** where we track, schedule, and execute all inspections and certifications, and provide you with a live audit trail for your own compliance reporting.
- **On-site liaison** — for larger estates, a dedicated point of contact who knows your sites, your people, and your operational constraints.

This model works across Hard Services (electrical, plumbing, reactive maintenance, fire safety) and Soft Services (facilities management, security coordination, catering support) — consolidating procurement and improving response times.

serviceHighlights.description: Integrated hard and soft services under one contract, with predictable budgets and scheduled maintenance reducing downtime and reactive costs.
Fire safety, electrical testing, water safety, H&S audits — all scheduled, executed, and documented for your own compliance reporting.
24/7 hotline with engineers dispatched to any of your sites within our response-time commitment, keeping your operations running.
Coordination with your internal security teams and integration of our security services across your site portfolio.
Monthly or quarterly reporting on spend, trends, and preventative work completed — helping you forecast and optimize building services budgets.
New build or lease assumption? We handle the fit-out services, compliance audit, and full documentation handover.

data.title: Healthcare
data.heroDescription: Critical infrastructure management for hospitals, clinics, and care facilities where downtime affects patient outcomes
data.overview:
Healthcare facilities operate 24/7 with zero tolerance for service failures. A plumbing issue, an electrical fault, or a fire safety system malfunction isn't just inconvenient — it can disrupt patient care, compromise sterile environments, and trigger regulatory scrutiny.

Atlas South understands the operational constraints of healthcare estates. Our engineers work within your infection control protocols, coordinate around clinical schedules, and respond to emergencies with the prioritization your facility requires.
data.challenges:
- **Zero-downtime mandate:** Unlike a typical office, you cannot simply "shut down" a wing for maintenance. Work must be coordinated around clinical operations, visiting hours, and patient transfer protocols.
- **Sterility and infection control:** Service engineers must understand your infection control zones, PPE requirements, and handover protocols — a standard tradesperson is not equipped for this.
- **Regulatory weight:** Health & Safety Executive (HSE), CQC, Fire & Rescue, environmental health, and your own governance committee all audit your building services and compliance records.
- **Critical systems:** Backup generators, emergency lighting, fire suppression, medical gas systems, water purity — failures ripple through clinical operations instantly.
- **Aging estates:** Many healthcare buildings are decades old with legacy infrastructure that requires specialist knowledge and careful planning to maintain without disrupting modern services running on top.
data.ourApproach:
We embed ourselves into your healthcare operational model, not the other way around:

- **Clinical-aware scheduling:** Maintenance is planned around clinical calendars, shift handovers, and patient flow — not imposed on you.
- **Infection control compliance:** Our engineers are briefed on your facility's IC protocols and understand the segregation of "clean" and "dirty" zones, decontamination workflows, and PPE requirements.
- **24/7 emergency response:** A senior, hospital-experienced engineer is dispatched to any critical system failure, and we coordinate with your facilities team and clinical leadership in real time.
- **Compliance documentation:** Every service visit, inspection, and maintenance event is recorded and cross-referenced to your compliance calendar — feeding directly into your CQC and HSE evidence files.
- **Legacy system expertise:** Older buildings often have mixed-age infrastructure. We maintain both vintage systems and newer additions without introducing incompatibilities or silent failures.

serviceHighlights.description: Senior engineers dispatched to critical infrastructure failures. Real-time coordination with clinical teams and facilities management.
Scheduled works planned around clinical operations, reducing the risk of emergency breakdowns affecting patient care.
Fire safety, electrical testing, water safety, medical gas systems — all documented for HSE, CQC, and internal governance audits.
Deep facility cleaning and infection control coordination, with protocols tailored to healthcare standards.
Integrated with your clinical security needs — controlled access to equipment rooms, pharmacy areas, and sensitive infrastructure.
Experience with older healthcare estate infrastructure, mixed-age systems, and the knowledge to maintain without disrupting modern overlays.

data.title: Retail
data.heroDescription: Keep customer-facing spaces operational, safe, and compliant while managing costs across multi-unit estates
data.overview:
Retail centres, flagship stores, and distributed retail chains share one overriding constraint: the building must be ready to serve customers every day the doors are open. A fire alarm fault, a water leak, or broken HVAC isn't just a maintenance issue — it's lost trading hours, customer experience damage, and potential evacuation.

Atlas South has managed retail estates ranging from single high-street stores to multi-unit regional portfolios, coordinating maintenance schedules around trading hours and tenant requirements.
data.challenges:
- **Trading hours constraints:** Most retail works must happen outside opening hours, creating a tight scheduling window and premium rates for any emergency overnight call.
- **Multi-tenant coordination:** If the building houses independent retailers, each has its own lease terms, insurance, and operational priorities — plus the landlord's broader infrastructure to manage.
- **Customer safety liability:** High footfall means high risk exposure. Any service failure affecting customer safety (trips, electrical hazards, fire safety) creates immediate liability and reputational risk.
- **Energy efficiency:** Retail spaces run heating, cooling, and lighting for long hours. A poorly maintained HVAC or lighting system drains profitability fast.
- **Specialist areas:** Retail chains often require food prep facilities, cold storage, secure areas, and specialist flooring — all with specific maintenance and compliance requirements.
data.ourApproach:
We structure retail support around the trading calendar, not against it:

- **Trading-hours aware scheduling:** Maintenance and inspections are coordinated outside opening hours, with weekend or overnight works available for time-critical issues.
- **Multi-site coordination:** Manage one portfolio across multiple locations with a single point of contact, reducing the overhead of coordinating with separate vendors per unit.
- **Tenant liaison:** For managed centres, we coordinate with tenant teams, manage insurance handovers, and handle the logistical complexity of working in occupied retail environments.
- **Compliance & safety:** Fire safety, electrical testing, and Health & Safety inspections stay on schedule, reducing liability exposure.
- **Cost optimization:** Preventative maintenance on HVAC, lighting, and water systems reduces emergency call-outs and keeps energy bills predictable.

serviceHighlights.description: Scheduled works outside trading hours, with emergency response available overnight and weekends for critical issues.
Single point of contact and coordination across multiple retail locations, reducing procurement overhead and improving response times.
Fire safety, electrical testing, gas safety, water systems — all scheduled and documented without disrupting customer experience.
HVAC optimization, lighting controls, and preventative maintenance to keep energy costs down across the estate.
Deep cleaning, post-incident remediation, and health & safety compliance cleaning for food/beverage areas.
Coordination with retail security systems, access control, and CCTV integration across your sites.

data.title: Education & Learning Institutions
data.heroDescription: Safe, compliant, and cost-effective building services for schools, universities, and training centres
data.overview:
Educational facilities are often multi-purpose environments serving hundreds or thousands of students, staff, and visitors daily. A single safety failure or unplanned closure affects education delivery, student welfare, and staff safety.

Atlas South works with schools, sixth forms, universities, and specialist training centres, managing building services around term schedules and balancing safety, compliance, and budget constraints.
data.challenges:
- **Duty of care:** Educational institutions have explicit safeguarding and duty of care responsibilities to students and staff. Any building safety issue (faulty wiring, poor ventilation, blocked fire exits) triggers immediate liability.
- **Budget constraints:** Educational budgets are typically tight, with competing priorities for teaching resources. Building services must deliver compliance and safety without excessive cost.
- **Term-time operations:** Schools operate on term calendars with holiday breaks. Maintenance must fit around school hours, exams, term ends, and break periods.
- **High-use environments:** Schools and universities pack intensive use into shared spaces — lecture halls, labs, kitchens, residences, sports facilities. Maintenance demand is high and wear predictable.
- **Regulatory oversight:** HSE, DfE, local authority inspections, and Ofsted all assess your facility management and safety record.
data.ourApproach:
We align building services with educational operations, not the reverse:

- **Term-aware scheduling:** Maintenance is planned around term calendars, holiday breaks, and exam schedules — minimizing disruption to teaching.
- **Preventative focus:** Regular inspections and scheduled maintenance reduce emergency breakdowns that force closures or disrupt learning.
- **Safety & compliance:** Fire safety, electrical testing, asbestos management (if applicable), water safety, and gas — all documented for HSE and Ofsted audits.
- **Budget transparency:** Fixed-price maintenance contracts deliver cost predictability for institutional budgets, with clear documentation for governors/trustees.
- **Emergency response:** When something breaks during term, we respond quickly and minimize impact on teaching and student welfare.

serviceHighlights.description: Maintenance scheduled around term calendars, exams, and holiday breaks to minimize disruption to teaching.
Regular inspections and scheduled works reduce emergency breakdowns that force closures or affect learning.
Fire safety, electrical testing, water quality, gas safety, and H&S audits — all documented for HSE, DfE, and Ofsted.
Fixed-price annual contracts for institutional budgets with clear documentation for governors, trustees, and finance teams.
Cleaning, catering support, security coordination, and day-to-day operations across the entire campus.
When urgent repairs are needed during term, we respond quickly and coordinate with teaching staff to minimize impact.
